articles.title: Programme structure
articles.summary: 13 online sessions, April–December, normally every third Thursday, 6:00–8:00 p.m. Sydney time. Guest presentation, Q&A and group discussion through Zoom.

articles.title: Participation and completion
articles.summary: Attend at least 10 of 13 sessions, complete written reflections and three viva voce reviews. Cameras remain on. Sessions are not recorded. The Chatham House Rule protects attribution. Conference entrants have a reported two-absence allowance; starting fellows three. Additional absences require a medical certificate.

articles.title: Applications and eligibility
articles.summary: Over 18; Australia or New Zealand; undergraduate, postgraduate, recent graduate or young professional, from any discipline. No prior economics or classical-liberal study required. High-school students are ineligible. Fellowship upper age limit is not published in the supplied source. The separate workshop’s 18–27 cap must not be assumed to apply.

articles.title: Funding and opportunities
articles.summary: Donor-funded participation with no fee. No stipend, salary, research grant, academic credit or CIS employment is established. Completion offers a certificate and access to the alumni network, internship opportunities, subsidised events and priority access to further programmes, without guaranteed jobs.
